The CLI-generated SDK declares NatsInCluster *bool, NatsReplicas *int and StreamMaxBytes *int on gcp.DispatchArgs (sdks/sjawhar-envoy-infra/envoyinfra/gcp/dispatch.go:105-175). Both valid rows — natsInCluster true with natsReplicas 5 and streamMaxBytes 1 (both bounds), and the SOCKS5 mode with neither number — reach `envoy-infra:gcp:Dispatch needs a "gcp" provider in its providers option`, the providers.Require gate the resolver runs before. Supplying a gcp and a random provider (registered by type, so no provider SDK is needed) takes the same program past that gate: the engine plans `+ 17 to create` and then fails on gcp:organizations/getProject for the fixture project, which is where this surface ends.

observations.what: O1 — a scheduling input for INFRA-553's apply, not a defect here: natsInCluster and natsUrl must change in one apply. With natsInCluster set and a natsUrl naming the hub's tailnet MagicDNS name — which is exactly what production carries today — the component renders happily with no proxy at all, and neither NATS client can then resolve its hub.
observations.evidence: Measured from this worker pod, an ordinary cluster pod with no tailscale sidecar: `getent hosts envoy-hub.<tailnet>.ts.net` exits 2 and resolves nothing, while `getent hosts envoy-hub.envoy.svc.cluster.local` answers the ClusterIP of Service envoy-hub in namespace envoy (`kubectl -n envoy get svc`). Production's two NATS clients each run in a pod with one container and no tailscale sidecar (`kubectl -n dispatch get pods -o json`: dispatch-57688ffbc9-twn97/envoy-dispatch, dispatch-listener-86498746bf-vv78w/envoy-listener), so the tailnet name works for them today only because ENVOY_NATS_SOCKS5_PROXY routes through the front-door pod, which is a tailnet node. My probe TestProbeInClusterAcceptsATailnetHubURL rendered natsInCluster with nats://envoy-hub.example-tailnet.ts.net:4222 and both containers came out with that URL and no ENVOY_NATS_SOCKS5_PROXY key at all.
observations.judgement: Not a failure of any acceptance criterion, and not pinned by a red test. The component refuses only what it can prove unreachable without resolving a name (bus.LocalNATSURL), and a blanket refusal of the deployment's own tailnet DNS name would refuse a cluster that forwards ts.net to a Tailscale nameserver, which is a real deployment shape. The hazard is stated three times in prose the operator meets — DispatchArgs.NatsInCluster's doc comment ('at an address their own cluster resolves'), the README's natsInCluster paragraph ('Point it at the hub's own Service, such as nats://envoy-hub.envoy.svc.cluster.local:4222') and the refusal message itself. Whether to make it machine-checkable is a design decision for the architect; sent to it.

observations.what: O2 — apply ordering, already owned by the tree as A1/INFRA-551, with evidence added: if natsInCluster is applied before the bridge's network policy admits namespace dispatch, the app rolls fully and serves without a bus while the listener's rollout stalls, rather than both failing loudly.
observations.evidence: envoy-dispatch's readiness reads only Postgres and reports nats false meanwhile, and its bus clients connect in the background (dispatch_kube.go, the comment above the front-door DependsOn, and README 'The pods'); envoy-listener exits on a failed initial connect (packages/envoy/cmd/listener/main.go), so its pods never go ready. Both Deployments roll with maxUnavailable 0 and maxSurge 1, so the listener's rollout holds its old pods while the app's completes.
observations.judgement: Not a defect of this change — the ordering is the architect's A1 — but the asymmetry is worth having in writing before the apply is scheduled. Sent to the architect.
